title: Entanglement renormalization, quantum error correction, and bulk causality
abstract: MERA read as an encoding circuit for a family of approximate quantum error correcting codes. Logical information is progressively better protected against erasure at larger length scales; an approximate holographic code emerges at low energy for critical systems; operators widely separated in scale obey a Lieb-Robinson type bound. Published JHEP 04 (2017) 040.
key_claims: All results are UPPER bounds on recovery error, powers of 2^(-nu), nu := -log2(Re lambda_1) of the scaling superoperator on an elementary block (Definition 2, RG-regular)
Lemma 3 (Eq. 4.1): decoupling of a simply connected region A from the reference, error <= C ||O|| 2^(-nu(s - log2|A|)); Theorem 2: local correctability from a shielding neighbourhood
Entanglement wedge reconstruction in this framework is left open: 'The approximate nature of our bound makes this analysis challenging'
Exact statements only in the nu -> infinity limit, which the authors say they do not expect to be physical; minimal logical support is Cantor-set type
